newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak on rate fears, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak on rate fears, off lows.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended the session weak on Monday, hit by fears of higher interest rates, but prices were off their lows by the close as bargain-hunters stepped in around support levels, analysts said.

The Hang Seng index fell 52.45 points to 11,106.57 after reaching a session low at 11,046.82. Turnover was a quiet HK$2.85 billion compared to HK$7.35 billion on Friday. Friday's volume was boosted by a New World Development share placement.
"Interest rates are the main concern right now - the market fell on rising interest rate concerns but volume was thin," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

Stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data released on Friday sparked fears of a near-term interest rate rise by the Federal Reserve, pushing the U.S. long bond down 30/32 to yield 7.12 percent. The Dow industrials fell 31.44 points to 5,616.21.
"It is almost sure that the Fed will raise interest rates at the next meeting judging from the figures released recently," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
Interest-rate sensitive financial stocks were hit hard on Monday with HSBC Holdings dropping HK$1.50 to HK$132.00.
Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.30 to HK$27.75 but Hang Seng Bank closed steady at HK$79.25.
"There is a lot of profit-taking and also higher interest rates are not good for banks," said Mak.
He said bargain-hunters had stepped in as the blue-chip index approached 11,000 points, allowing stocks to close above their lows. "11,000 is near-term support," he said.

Analysts said the market was likely to see low turnover again on Tuesday, with Wall Street closed for Labour Day on Monday and unable to provide direction. "Tomorrow I think it is most likely to just move sideways," said Tsang.
Shares of First Pacific Ltd ended HK$0.20 lower at HK$12.35 after the company posted interim earnings of US$90.8 million compared with US$129.1 million the year-ago period.

China-funded oil explorer CNPC (Hong Kong) rose HK$0.05 to HK$0.375 after the United Nations said it would delay plans to implement an oil-for-food deal with Iraq, brokers said. They said there was also speculation the company was planning to buy oilfields in Southeast Asia
Shanghai Industrial shares rose HK$0.30 to HK$14.00. The company is due to report interim results on Tuesday.
September Hang Seng futures fell 15 points to 11,080.
